title: So much theatre!! Which shows are you most excited for?? 👀 #theatre #...
transcript: here's an epic roundup of theatre opening in New York this winter, that I think should be on your radar if you find this helpful, I post these big roundups 4 times a year plus I got really good feedback on my “what's closing in November” video so the December video is coming soon too, by popular demand so I divided these shows up into these five categories: 1) shows I've already seen and recommend 2) celebrities onstage 3) musicals 4) exciting plays and saving the best for last, a category I'm calling 5) weird and wonderful as always if I missed anything you're excited about please tell me and I'll probably add to the comments as I find out about things too but without further ado the first show I've already seen and highly recommend my favorite show of 2024 Burnout Paradise is returning to New York the performers are on treadmills and they try to accomplish a series of tasks with the audience's help it's kind of a commentary on grind culture Cold War Choir practice is returning after a hit run at Clubbed Thumb this summer it's a very heightened imaginative spy comedy / play with music satire on the Red Scare through the eyes of a Black American child and Hold on to Your Butts a sort of parody show where they reenact Jurassic Park but with everyday objects instead of big effects moving into the celebrities onstage category we gotta start with one of the most stacked cast we've had all year this revival of Tartuffe not to be confused with the one that Andre De Shields was in this new version by Lucas Hnath stars Matthew Broderick, David Cross and a huge line up of theatre favorites my beloved Daniel Radcliffe is coming back to Broadway in a revival of the solo play Every Brilliant Thing which I've only heard excellent things about national treasure June Squibb is coming back to the stage in a revival of the Pulitzer finalist play, Marjorie Prime alongside Cynthia Nixon and Danny Burstein we got Michelle Williams starring in Eugene O'Neill's Anna Christie directed by her husband Thomas KaIl and speaking of real life couples Carrie Coon is gonna be in a revival of Bug by her husband Tracy Letts Does Ethan Slater count as a celebrity now? sure, why not? he's actually co-writing and starring in Marcel on the Train a true story about a French mime who rescued Jewish children during WW2 Sean Hayes is doing the Unknown by David Cale making it the 2nd solo play this season written by David Cale about a writer retreating to a remote area but this one appears to be more of a thriller All Out is a follow up to last year's somewhat controversial show All In where a rotating cast of celebrities read stories written by Simon Rich a lot of people last year were not happy to find out what the format of the show was but I don't know maybe everyone's on the same page now I hear tickets are not quite as insanely expensive as before I don't know though and there are still some exciting celebrity names here so for what it's worth next we have two different plays inspired by Antigone the Other Place starring Emma Darcy from House of the Dragon and the other one is Antigone (this play I read in high school) starring Tony Shalhoub and Celia Keenan-Bolger we have this play called a Data starring a few people you might recognise from film and TV especially if you're on the younger side but most exciting for me is Sophia Lillis whose work I've really enjoyed on screen so I'm excited to see her on stage this one appears to be a sort of topical story taking place in Silicon Valley let's talk about some musicals playing this winter starting with Bigfoot which is co-written by Amber Ruffin there's an adaptation of Picnic at Hanging Rock which I've never read but I saw a play adaptation of it once and I found the story extremely haunting Encores is doing High Spirits based on the Noel Coward play Blithe Spirit starring another real life couple Steven Pasquale and Philippa Soo as well as Tony winners Katrina Lenk and Andrea Martin and LCT is partnering with the Met Opera to do an intimate revival of the family opera Ahmal and the Night Visitors I also highly recommend checking out the Prototype Festival which does experimental opera and music theatre pieces when I've seen their shows they've ended up being some of my favorites of the year moving back to non-musicals we have a production of Coriolanus which incorporates the theme of video game violence or something sounds interesting! and we have a number of exciting new plays like Mother Russia by Lauren Yee who you might know from Cambodian Rock Band and this is a dark comedy taking place after the fall of the Soviet Union The Dinosaurs about a group of women who regularly meet to “share stories of recovery” but it seems to be on kind of a blurred timeline like maybe taking place over the course of centuries or millennia the Disappear, a new comedy by Erica Schmidt described as being about a “power couple whose picture perfect life goes gloriously off script” We got the Monsters by Ngozi Anyanwu also, starring Oak Onaodowan and it's described as a sibling love story Chinese Republicans by Alex Lin about a group of “high powered businesswomen” who react and adjust when a younger woman joins their company and my final category: weird and wonderful obviously I haven't seen any of these shows yet so I don't know if they're wonderful but they seem kooky and strange in a way that I'll love and are maybe harder to categorize neatly starting off with What if They Ate the Baby? by the clown duo Xhloe and Natasha coming off their hit show A Letter to Lyndon B Johnson or God this one seems to be a play on old fashioned housewives and I'm really excited for Gooey's Toxic Aquatic Adventure which is like a mermaid puppet musical honestly pause and read the description ‘Cause I can't do it justice we've got the F*gg*ts and their Friends Between Revolutions which appears to be an interpretive reimagining of the 1977 gay manifesto book by Larry Mitchell of the same name we got Meat Suit or The Sh!tshow of motherhood a performance piece by Aya Ogawa described as a “genre-defying theatrical carnival” I saw her show The Nosebleed some years ago and I thought it was really beautiful and inventive so I'm excited to see what she's up to next we've got DIRT which is like part interactive theatre, part game where you collectively reimagine a model of Manhattan with like all sorts of building materials or something I don't know it sounds super fun Edelweiss is like a theatrical spin on Christmas pageants and it's by the same theatre company that did the bizarre but delightful play the Beastiary last year at Ars Nova, which I loved and finally, I'll leave you on the cliffhanger that I'm probably gonna do a separate video about the most wonderful time of the year the Under the Radar Festival and I just gotta say if you like cool and exciting theatre and you're not paying attention to Under the Radar, then what are you doing?
classificationReason: Self-described 'epic roundup' of NYC theatre opening this winter, spanning five categories and multiple shows (Burnout Paradise, Cold War Choir Practice, Hold On To Your Butts, and more).
